title: Richer input: the reader, more than 9 letters at once, and making EmbeddingGemma beat the letter reader

brief.state:
Snapshot checked 2026-10-07 against the files (no live PC runs). B2 = 3,302,481 params: reader = 108 hand-listed chars + hand place code + 2 conv blocks (kernel 5, so a +-4 letter window, no attention); thinker = 2 blocks, 8 fixed rounds, 17 state vectors (8 control, 9 register), attending to every reader position each round; exact int64 executor; pointer-generator talker. Six paired seeds (200-205, PC, q33): pooled-5 mean 74.02 (73.00-74.74) over 6,040 rows; chain-5 99.4-99.7; B2 minus plain_tf +20.34 (6/6 seeds); B2 minus plain_tf_steps +6.89 (6/6). B2 gets about 35% of the variant split and 1.6% of the four unseen-kind family split.

Gemma arms (2-seed screens, same-box B2V baselines 73.48 and 74.39): EGE (Gemma before the window; whole model 274.5M, trainable 3.50M) gives +1.59/+2.12. It passes pooled, chain and every split on average, but fails the variant mark (+1.70 vs +3.0) and the loops:0 leak (18.09 on seed 200). EGK: seed 200 finished (+0.97); seed 201 was non-finite in both runs. EGR, EGO, EGM and EGW (Gemma without the window) lost 0.3 to 5.3 points. EGT and Test LR were small and failed. The 6-seed EGE confirm (q39, seeds 202-207) is staged; no result files exist, and addendum 15 makes running it Ben's call.

Diagnosis (shown): Gemma's final state reads 23.0% of letters linearly; 99.6% of letters sit inside multi-letter pieces. With the in-piece offset and a 2-layer MLP it reads 97.4%, which needs tokenizer alignment. B2's reader reads 99.85% linearly. D0 shows the reader window reads every digit place at 99.997% or better, but the executor never reads the reader: its operands are regex int() values.

Built but not run: W1 (one low-rank attention block, 3,336,113 params, queue 42 after U0), U0 (BPE prompt on plain_tf_steps, 3,339,776, queue 41; its base truncates steps at 64 chars, which conflicts with rule 7), C0 (cap 107, queue 43), T1 (calculator outside, 3,277,393, queue 40). Not built: U2 (no code, no queue) and V1 raw bytes (+41,377 params, beyond the 39,399 headroom). Main gaps for richer input: W1 is untested, the number and word tokenizers on the input path are hand-written, and the Gemma arms are judged only against B2 (3.3M), not a same-size model.

open_questions: Which size baseline applies to Gemma arms? Ben's rule 3 says size comparisons count borrowed parts and compare with plain transformers of the same size (+-3%). PASS-MARKS addendum 4 instead calls EGE (274.5M) a B2-internal result. A claim that the Gemma reader beats the scratch reader needs a same-size plain model (about 274M), which has not been run. Which rule governs?

Is hand code on the input path allowed? Examples: the number regex and int() (ledger.py:199-208), word_spans used by the place code and WORD copy (reader.py:21, ledger.py:209, 383-394), and EGE's character-to-token alignment via tokenizer offsets (eg.py:51-67). Is the fixed +-4 letter window (kernel 5, two blocks) a hand-chosen part under rules 0 and 4? Ben calls it test-fitting. R0's loss is confounded with 19.9% fewer parameters, and no size-matched control has been run.
Should EGE's 6-seed confirm (q39) run? Addendum 15 says it is Ben's call and is removed if he says stop.

Rule 7 conflict in U0: its base plain_tf_steps (cap 64) trains 840 var_chain rows answer-only. Should U0 be re-staged on C0 (cap 107) before its verdict is used, or is the 64-cap base accepted as an exception?

Digits: the reader can read digits (D0 PASS), but the executor reads regex int() values, so reader digits never reach the calculator. Is T1's text call route meant to be the digit route, given it still uses regex spans to find numbers?

distinct.title: Same-size 274M plain baseline: 200-step timing probe first
distinct.summary: Rule 3 asks for a plain transformer of the same size as EGE's whole 274.5M. None exists (largest plain run 10.8M). A 200-step timing and memory probe on the PC sizes one run before any commitment; the full run would be plain_tf_steps at d=1280, L=14, cap 107 (about 276M) with gradient accumulation.
distinct.change: New baseline plain_tf_steps d_model 1280, 14 layers, 20 heads, cap 107 (no answer-only rows); trainer changes: micro-batch 32 x 8 accumulation (train.py:171-173 steps once per batch), length bucketing; lr 3e-4 sealed in an addendum; new size band in the addendum (train.py's 3.14-3.34M check would print inside=False). Timing probe: 200 steps, projected hours and peak memory.
distinct.why: Only a same-size plain model can show whether Gemma beats scratch at equal total size. FLOP estimates differ: 17-33 h per 24k-step seed on the 5070 Ti without bucketing (this idea) vs about 9.4 h on the calibration box (FLOP scaling from the 10.8M run) — both untested. The cheaper rungs of the shrink ladder have affordable comparators, so run those first. The 8a first look shows B2's lead over plain shrinking from 3M to 10M (4.2/4.5 from 5.5/7.0), another reason to compare at the real size.

distinct.title: Self-gated reading after deployment, reader only
distinct.summary: After shipping, the thinker stays frozen and the reader (letter table excluded) keeps learning from free text the model fetches through an outside tool. The model picks the window it finds hardest, keeps an update only if its own held-out masked-letter loss does not rise and its own skills self-test does not fall, and stops when a round accepts nothing. It is the only deploy-time learning idea in this area.
distinct.change: A deploy loop around the B2 checkpoint, no architecture change. Each round: fetch 64 FineWeb windows through a tool (protected-hash filter inside the tool); score each by the reader's masked-span loss; take one gradient step on the highest-loss window; accept only if (a) masked loss on a replay set the model built from its own earlier reads does not rise and (b) accuracy on a fresh skills batch from an outside generator tool does not fall; stop when no window is accepted. Freeze reader.tok so the talker's output does not move.
distinct.why: The reader is 22% of B2 (742,400 params) and every thinker round reads it, so drift can move skills accuracy; the self-test gate is the guard. If reading helps, expected movers are frame and vocab as in the cloze idea.
